original_question: Quantify the aging phenomenon of ideal fluids, preferably by constructing a Lyapunov function on fluid velocities that is nondecreasing along Euler evolution except on a slim exceptional set.
target_in_paper: Problem 22 (Aging Problem) in §8.2, 'Aging of the fluid, irreversibility and Lyapunov functions,' within the section 'Long time behaviour of 2D flows.' ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it identifies the 'aging' phenomenon for ideal incompressible Euler flow, it keeps the paper's preferred mechanism of a Lyapunov function on velocity fields, and it matches the stated monotonicity requirement along Euler evolution with equality only on a 'slim' exceptional set. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's setting here is not arbitrary dimension: §8 is explicitly about long-time behaviour of 2D flows, and §8.1 fixes M to be a compact two-dimensional manifold, possibly with boundary. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

'Ideal fluid' must be unpacked as the incompressible, inviscid Euler equation on M, with velocity tangent to the boundary when ∂M is nonempty. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The unknown should be written as a global 2D Euler solution u=u(t,x) of (1.1), since Problem 22 is phrased for an arbitrary Euler solution u(t,x) and asks about comparing velocity fields at two times t1 and t2. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The Lyapunov function is not merely 'on fluid velocities' abstractly: the paper asks for L to be defined and continuous on the space of velocities T_e D^s_μ(M). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

To make T_e D^s_μ(M) stand-alone, one should say that D^s_μ(M) is the H^s Sobolev completion of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group D_μ(M), so T_e D^s_μ(M) is the H^s space of divergence-free velocity fields (tangent to ∂M when relevant); in 2D the local well-posedness discussion uses s>n/2+1, hence s>2. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The monotonicity condition should be stated exactly as d/dt L(u(t,·)) ≥ 0 along every such Euler solution, not just informally as 'nondecreasing along Euler evolution.' ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The exceptional set should be localized precisely: equality is to hold only on a 'slim' subset of T_e D^s_μ(M), with the paper suggesting 'say, of infinite codimension' as the intended meaning. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The motivating interpretation should be retained if one wants full faithfulness: the problem asks whether one can tell, from u(t1,·) and u(t2,·), which state is earlier, i.e. whether aging can be read off from the velocity field itself. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The paper frames this as an open problem, not as a theorem or conjecture, and your rewrite should stay at that level. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
refined_question: Let M be a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold, possibly with boundary, with volume form μ, and let D^s_μ(M) denote the H^s Sobolev completion of the group D_μ(M) of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, for some s>2, so that T_e D^s_μ(M) is the H^s space of divergence-free velocity fields on M tangent to ∂M when ∂M≠∅. For a global solution u=u(t,x) of the incompressible Euler equations ∂_t u + u·∇u = -∇p, div u = 0 on M, is it possible to quantify the fluid's 'aging' by constructing a continuous Lyapunov function L:T_e D^s_μ(M)→R such that d/dt L(u(t,·)) ≥ 0 along every Euler trajectory, with equality only on a slim subset of T_e D^s_μ(M) (for example, a subset of infinite codimension), thereby allowing one to distinguish which of two velocity fields u(t1,·) and u(t2,·) corresponds to the earlier time? ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets §8.2 rather than the paper's earlier conjectural material, because the distinctive phrases 'aging', 'Lyapunov function', and 'slim' exceptional set occur together precisely in Problem 22. The nearby context in §8 and §8.1 supplies the hidden 2D compact-manifold setting, while §1 and §5.2 provide the Euler equation, the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group D_μ(M), and its Sobolev completion D^s_μ(M). I therefore kept the question narrow, faithful to the paper's official formulation, and did not replace it by the more concrete periodic-channel 'kink' persistence question of Problem 23 or by any broader irreversibility/entropy problem. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
